title: Clarify — Just to make sure we're on the same page…

meaning.en: To make something easier to understand.
meaning.fil: Linawin ang impormasyon para mas madaling maintindihan.

examples.everyday: Could you clarify where we should meet?

options: To make something easier to understand.
check.explanation: Clarify means: To make something easier to understand. Example: Could you clarify the deadline?
check.hint: Think about how "clarify" is used in this example: Could you clarify the deadline?

explanation.en: To make something easier to understand. For example: Could you clarify the deadline?
explanation.taglish: Ginagamit ito kapag gusto mong siguraduhin na pareho ang pagkaintindi ninyo.
explanation.fil: Linawin ang impormasyon para mas madaling maintindihan.

phrase.text: Just to make sure we're on the same page…

meaning.taglish: I-check kung pareho kayo ng understanding.
meaning.fil: Ginagamit kapag may kailangang linawin bago magtrabaho.
meaning.en: To politely confirm that everyone understands the same plan.

examples.work: Just to make sure we're on the same page, the report is due Friday, right?
examples.everyday: Just to make sure we're on the same page, are we meeting at three?

dialogue.speaker: Coworker
dialogue.text: Who will submit the revised report?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Just to make sure we're on the same page, I'll submit the report after you check it. Is that correct?

dialogue.speaker: Coworker
dialogue.text: Yes. You'll submit it after I check the formatting.

check.prompt: When should you use this phrase?
check.explanation: To politely confirm that everyone understands the same plan. Example: Just to make sure we're on the same page, the report is due Friday, right?
check.hint: Read the complete example aloud: Just to make sure we're on the same page, the report is due Friday, right?

grammarTip.explanation: Use 'Could you + base verb...?' for a polite request: 'Could you clarify the deadline?' Sa polite request, 'clarify' lang, hindi 'clarifies'.

speaking.scenario: Your supervisor asks you to confirm who will submit a report. Ask politely and restate the agreed plan.
hints: Could you clarify who will ___? I'll ___ by ___. Is that correct?
Use your own details or imagine a situation. Pauses are okay.
A short clear message is enough; add details only if useful.
speaking.oneMinuteGoal: Use the sentence starter to give a clear message with one useful detail. Stop when your message is complete, even before one minute.
speaking.twoMinuteGoal: Optional extension: add a reason, an example, or a next step. You do not need to fill two minutes.
speaking.modelResponse: Just to make sure we're on the same page, I'll submit the report on Friday after you check the formatting. Is that correct? Please let me know if someone else will send it.
selfReview: I answered the situation with a clear main message.
I included the detail or question the listener needs.
I chose one sentence to improve or practice again.
preparationQuestions: What detail will make it clear?

durationGuidance.en: One and two minutes are optional practice targets, not minimums. A shorter complete message counts. Start with two or three sentences, then add detail if useful.
durationGuidance.taglish: Optional targets lang ang isa o dalawang minuto. Puwedeng mas maikli basta malinaw ang mensahe. Magsimula sa dalawa o tatlong pangungusap.
durationGuidance.fil: Gabay lamang ang isa o dalawang minuto, hindi kailangang abutin. Sapat ang mas maikling sagot kung malinaw ang mensahe.

speaking.modelResponseNote: This is one short example, not a script to memorize or a timed one-minute answer. Your details and wording may differ.
